catalyst_text: Presented new data showing improved event free survival
detailed_catalyst_text: An analysis in progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis showed improved event-free survival for patients treated with the medicine versus a real-world external cohort from the NAPPED database. Benefits were observed for time to surgical biliary diversion and to liver transplantation or death. Results add evidence for long-term effectiveness in this population.
catalyst_text_evidence: This analysis compared time to first clinical event between PFIC patients aged ≥1 year with non-truncating BSEP deficiency and FIC1 variants treated with LIVMARLI (maralixibat) for up to 4.8 years (n=41) and an external control cohort from the NAtural Course and Prognosis of PFIC and Effect of Biliary Diversion (NAPPED) database (n=256). The LIVMARLI (maralixibat)-treated cohort showed significant improvement in overall EFS (HR=0.29; 95% CI 0.16-0.54; p=0.0001) as well as in EFS for SBD (HR=0.05 (95% CI 0.01-0.39), p=0.0036) and for liver transplantation or death (HR=0.44 (95% CI 0.22-0.88), p=0.02), respectively.

catalyst_text: Positive Phase 2b results reported in hepatitis delta
detailed_catalyst_text: Phase 2b AZURE-1 data in chronic hepatitis delta virus infection demonstrated strong antiviral activity with high virologic response rates and ALT normalization versus delayed treatment. The composite primary endpoint was achieved in both dosing arms, and treatment was well tolerated. Findings included patients with advanced disease characteristics.
catalyst_text_evidence: At Week 24, treatment with brelovitug resulted in virologic response (≥2 log10 reduction in HDV RNA from baseline or undetectable HDV RNA [<LLOQ, TND]) rates of 100% in the 300 mg once weekly (QW) arm and 75% in the 900 mg once every four weeks (Q4W) arm, with ALT normalization achieved in 45% and 40% of patients, respectively, compared to 0% for both endpoints in the delayed treatment arm. The primary composite endpoint of virologic response and ALT normalization at Week 24 was achieved in 45% and 35% of patients in the 300 mg QW and 900 mg Q4W arms, respectively, versus 0% in the delayed treatment arm.

catalyst_text: Phase 2b study met primary endpoint in PSC
detailed_catalyst_text: Late-breaking Phase 2b VISTAS results in primary sclerosing cholangitis showed significant pruritus reductions versus placebo in patients with moderate-to-severe itch at baseline. The primary endpoint of cholestatic pruritus improvement was robustly met, with additional signals on serum bile acids and patient-reported outcomes. These data support therapeutic potential for managing pruritus in this cholestatic disease.
catalyst_text_evidence: Late-breaking results from the Phase 2b VISTAS study of volixibat in PSC and Phase 2b AZURE-1 study of brelovitug in HDV, alongside data featuring its established therapy, LIVMARLI (maralixibat), in PFIC, were presented at the European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL) International Liver Congress 2026. In 2026, Mirum shared that the Phase 2b VISTAS study of volixibat in PSC met its primary endpoint, with statistically significant and clinically meaningful reductions in pruritus observed in patients treated with volixibat.

catalyst_text: Trial met primary endpoint with clinically meaningful improvements
detailed_catalyst_text: Phase 2b VISTAS results in primary sclerosing cholangitis showed rapid, sustained, and clinically meaningful reductions in pruritus. The study met its primary endpoint, indicating symptomatic benefit for patients with moderate-to-severe itch. These outcomes support further development of the IBAT inhibitor in adult cholestatic disease.
catalyst_text_evidence: Late-breaking VISTAS results demonstrate rapid, sustained, and clinically meaningful reductions in pruritus with volixibat in primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC). In 2026, Mirum shared that the Phase 2b VISTAS study of volixibat in PSC met its primary endpoint, with statistically significant and clinically meaningful reductions in pruritus observed in patients treated with volixibat.

catalyst_text: Trial met composite endpoint with strong antiviral activity
detailed_catalyst_text: Phase 2b AZURE-1 results in chronic hepatitis delta virus demonstrated efficacy and safety. The study achieved the primary composite endpoint of virologic response and ALT normalization at Week 24, with strong antiviral activity observed. These data reinforce the therapeutic potential of the monoclonal antibody in HDV.
catalyst_text_evidence: Late-breaking Phase 2b AZURE-1 results demonstrate efficacy and safety of brelovitug for the treatment of chronic hepatitis delta virus (HDV). In 2026, Mirum announced that in the Phase 2b portion of the AZURE-1 study in HDV, treatment with brelovitug demonstrated strong antiviral activity in HDV and achieved the primary composite endpoint of virologic response and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) normalization at Week 24 in both brelovitug dose arms as compared to the delayed treatment arm.

catalyst_text: Phase 2b topline results positive primary endpoint met
detailed_catalyst_text: Announced positive topline results from the Phase 2b VISTAS study in primary sclerosing cholangitis, meeting the primary endpoint on the Adult ItchRO scale with a significant reduction in cholestatic pruritus. These data provide clinical proof-of-concept in PSC, a setting with no approved therapies for pruritus, signaling meaningful therapeutic potential.
catalyst_text_evidence: Mirum Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ:MIRM), a leading rare disease company, today announced the primary endpoint was met in the VISTAS Phase 2b study evaluating volixibat, an investigational oral ileal bile acid transporter (IBAT) inhibitor, in patients with primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC). In the primary analysis cohort, treatment with volixibat demonstrated a robust 2.72 point improvement in pruritus and a placebo-adjusted difference of 1.64 points in the primary endpoint (p<0.0001), as measured by the Adult ItchRO scale, reflecting change from baseline to the average of the last 12 weeks of treatment.

catalyst_text: Phase 2b primary endpoint met with robust activity
detailed_catalyst_text: The Phase 2b portion of the AZURE-1 study in chronic hepatitis delta virus met its primary composite endpoint at Week 24 across both dosing regimens, showing high virologic response rates and ALT normalization versus delayed treatment. Treatment was well tolerated with no discontinuations and no treatment-related serious adverse events. These data support the potential of the therapy as a single-agent option for HDV and continued advancement of the registrational program.
catalyst_text_evidence: Mirum Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ:MIRM), a leading rare disease company, today announced the primary endpoint was met in the Phase 2b portion of the AZURE-1 study evaluating brelovitug, an investigational monoclonal antibody designed to bind hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), for the treatment of chronic hepatitis delta virus (HDV). At Week 24, treatment with brelovitug demonstrated robust antiviral activity across both dose groups. 100% of patients in the 300 mg once weekly (QW) arm and 75% of patients in the 900 mg once every four weeks (Q4W) arm achieved virologic response (≥2 log10 reduction in HDV RNA from baseline or undetectable HDV RNA [<LLOQ, TND]), as compared to 0% in the delayed treatment arm. Consistent with these antiviral effects, the primary composite endpoint of virologic response and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) normalization was achieved in 45% and 35% of patients in the 300 mg QW and 900 mg Q4W arms, respectively, as compared to 0% of patients in the delayed treatment arm. Treatment with brelovitug was well tolerated across dose groups.

drug_indication: Cholestatic pruritus in rare cholestatic liver diseases
catalyst_text: Phase 3 enrollment completed topline data expected Q4
detailed_catalyst_text: Enrollment was completed for the Phase 3 EXPAND study evaluating maralixibat in patients with cholestatic pruritus due to rare cholestatic liver diseases, including biliary atresia. This milestone advances the registrational program aimed at potential label expansion into additional pruritus settings. Topline readout is planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.
catalyst_text_evidence: Mirum Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ:MIRM), a leading rare disease company, today announced completion of enrollment in EXPAND, a Phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study evaluating LIVMARLI® (maralixibat) for the treatment of cholestatic pruritus in patients aged 6 months or older with rare cholestatic liver diseases, including biliary atresia. Topline data from the EXPAND study are expected in the fourth quarter of 2026.

catalyst_text: Phase 3 enrollment complete and screening complete
detailed_catalyst_text: Enrollment in the Phase 3 AZURE-1 study was completed and screening in the Phase 3 AZURE-4 study was completed, both in treatment-naïve chronic hepatitis delta virus patients. These registrational milestones advance the pivotal program toward readouts and potential regulatory submissions.
catalyst_text_evidence: Mirum Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ:MIRM), a leading rare disease company, today announced completion of enrollment in the Phase 3 AZURE-1 study and completion of screening in the Phase 3 AZURE-4 study, both evaluating brelovitug for the treatment of chronic hepatitis delta virus (HDV).

catalyst_text: Initiated Phase 2 trial in Fragile X syndrome
detailed_catalyst_text: Initiation of the BLOOM Phase 2 clinical study in Fragile X syndrome was reported, evaluating MRM-3379, a selective PDE4D inhibitor. This advances the program into mid-stage patient testing to assess efficacy and safety in a disorder with no approved therapies targeting underlying biology.
catalyst_text_evidence: “Enthorin Therapeutics, LLC, a biotechnology company focused on circuit-modulating treatments for neurological and neurodevelopmental disorders, announced that its licensing partner for MRM-3379 (formerly ENT-3379), Mirum Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ:MIRM), in December, reported the initiation of the BLOOM Phase 2 clinical study evaluating MRM-3379 in Fragile X syndrome (FXS).” “The entry of MRM-3379 into Fragile X patient trials by Mirum Pharmaceuticals is the culmination of over a decade of diligent scientific research and development by the clinicians and scientists at Enthorin and DNS.”

catalyst_text: First participant enrolled in Phase 2 study
detailed_catalyst_text: The first participant was enrolled in the BLOOM Phase 2 study evaluating MRM-3379 for Fragile X Syndrome. The trial assesses safety, tolerability, and potential clinical benefit in males with genetically confirmed FXS, indicating that mid-stage development is underway.

The Phase 2b data indicated that the trial failed to achieve its primary and secondary endpoints, as reported on December 18, 2023.
The data from Phase 3 achieved the primary endpoint of significantly lowering bile alcohols (urine 23S-pentol), as reported on October 2, 2023.
